speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Priya, thanks so much for making the time. Can you hear me okay?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, loud and clear. Sorry in advance, the dog might bark at some point.

speaker: interviewer
text: No problem at all. So this is just about your grocery orders, there are no wrong answers.

speaker: interviewee
text: Sure, happy to help.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: So it's me, my husband Raj, and our two boys, they're seven and ten. I do most of the shopping. Raj works shifts at the hospital, so his week is all over the place. I usually go Saturday mornings to the big supermarket by the ring road.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: A mum from school had a referral code, she posted it in the class group chat. Ten off your first order or something like that.

speaker: interviewer
text: Nice. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: So that was a few weeks back. My little one had a proper fever that week and I could not drag him round a supermarket, so I sat on the sofa with him and did the whole thing on my phone. Bananas, crackers, those electrolyte drinks, soup. Then the normal stuff too, milk, bread, cereal. It took maybe twenty minutes, the search was a bit slow. Once he was better we were straight back to Saturdays at the big shop, to be honest.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Not often. I've tried a couple of the other apps over the years, but mostly I like to see the stuff myself, especially fruit.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. And when you do, is it the weekend or during the week?

speaker: interviewee
text: During the week, if at all. Weekends I'm in the shop anyway with the boys.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: On that order, the crackers. They were out of the ones he likes, so I got some other brand. He complained but he ate them. And the milk was a different brand, which, fine, milk is milk.

speaker: interviewer
text: And did you know about the swaps before the bags arrived?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I saw it when the bags came in. There was a little paper slip on top. I didn't really mind honestly, I had other things on my mind.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: There's a whiteboard on the fridge. In theory everyone writes on it. In practice it's me, and sometimes the ten-year-old writes chocolate in big letters.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Does your husband add things?

speaker: interviewee
text: Rarely. He texts me if he notices we're out of coffee. That's about it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I just took the first one that was the same day, I think it was four to six. I was home anyway, so it didn't really matter.

speaker: interviewer
text: And was that easy to find in the app?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, the same-day ones were right at the top. Easy.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on to the next one. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: A pass? For me, I don't think so. I'd have to order every week for it to make sense, and I don't.

speaker: interviewer
text: What if it was 9.99 a month with free delivery on everything?

speaker: interviewee
text: Still no, I think. Maybe for someone who does a big weekly order. Not us.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, probably. The driver was really polite, he carried the bags right into the kitchen.

speaker: interviewer
text: That's great to hear. What did you like most about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: The tracking. I could see him on the map, so I wasn't hovering by the front door.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. And anything you didn't like?

speaker: interviewee
text: The search. If you type crackers you get two hundred things and half of them aren't crackers.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, noted, search. Great. Did you use the app on your phone or on a computer?

speaker: interviewee
text: Phone. Always the phone.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. And did you get any emails from us after the order?

speaker: interviewee
text: I think so? A survey maybe. I don't really open those, sorry.

speaker: interviewer
text: No worries at all. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: Hmm, no, I think you covered it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Wonderful. Thank you so much Priya, this was really helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: No problem, good luck with it all.
